title: Filtered colimits and derived tensor in the second factor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A$ be a commutative $R$-algebra, let $M$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and for a complex $N$ of $R$-modules write $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ for the value $N\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M\in D(A)$ of the exact functor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M:D(R)\to D(A)$ of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (2) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so that a morphism $N\to N'$ of complexes of $R$-modules induces an $A$-linear map $H^n(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)\to H^n(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N')$. Let $I$ be a filtered category, let $(N_i)_{i\in I}$ be a diagram of complexes of $R$-modules indexed by $I$, and let $N=\varinjlim_i N_i$ be its termwise colimit with coprojections $\iota_j:N_j\to N$. Then for every integer $n$ the maps $H^n(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\iota_j)$ induce an isomorphism of $A$-modules $\varinjlim_i H^n(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N_i)\to H^n(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)$, natural in $M$ (for morphisms of complexes of $A$-modules) and in the diagram.

source.place: Tags 06YR and 06Y6: for a K-flat R-resolution E of M, Tot(E (x)_R -) commutes with filtered colimits termwise and cohomology commutes with filtered colimits (exactness of filtered colimits)

proof.text: Regard $M$ as a complex of $R$-modules and choose a K-flat $R$-resolution $e:E\to M$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For any complex $T$ of $R$-modules choose a K-flat $R$-resolution $f:F\to T$. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] represents $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}T$ in $D(A)$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R M)$, with its strict $A$-action through $M$. After forgetting the $A$-action, the two maps $$\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R M)\xleftarrow{1_F\otimes e}\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R E)\xrightarrow{f\otimes 1_E}\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_R E)$$ are quasi-isomorphisms of $R$-complexes. Indeed, the cones of $e$ and $f$ are acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]; the cone of each tensor map is its tensor with that acyclic cone by [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso], up to the sign symmetry of total tensor complexes. The K-flatness of $F$ and $E$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes both tensor cones acyclic. Thus this zigzag gives a canonical identification in $D(R)$ between the underlying complex of $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}T$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes_R E)$.

Apply Step 1 to every $T=N_i$ and to $T=N$. The comparison zigzags commute with every chain map $T\to T'$ when the same resolution $E\to M$ is held fixed: the total tensor maps $1_F\otimes e$ and $f\otimes 1_E$ are natural for maps of resolutions, and the canonical comparison between K-flat resolutions in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (2) removes the choices of $F$. Consequently the maps induced by $\iota_i$ correspond in $D(R)$ to the actual chain maps $\operatorname{Tot}(N_i\otimes_R E)\to\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_R E)$. On the one-point site, [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] gives a chain isomorphism $$\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Tot}(N_i\otimes_R E)\cong\operatorname{Tot}((\varinjlim_iN_i)\otimes_R E)=\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_R E),$$ under which the structure maps are precisely $\operatorname{Tot}(\iota_i\otimes 1_E)$.

source.place: Tag 06YR, proof, termwise tensor-colimit interchange; specialized here to modules on the one-point site

proof.text: The exactness clause of [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] on the one-point site says filtered colimits of $R$-modules are exact. Apply it in the three consecutive degrees $n-1,n,n+1$ of the complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(N_i\otimes_R E)$: exactness preserves the kernel of $d^n$ and the image of $d^{n-1}$, so it identifies $\varinjlim_i\ker(d_i^n)/\operatorname{im}(d_i^{n-1})$ with $\ker(d^n)/\operatorname{im}(d^{n-1})$. With Step 2 this is the canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_iH^n(\operatorname{Tot}(N_i\otimes_R E))\cong H^n(\operatorname{Tot}(N\otimes_R E))$ of $R$-modules. The calculation is valid for every integer $n$ without boundedness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 00DB (directed colimits commute with homology), applied degreewise to filtered diagrams

proof.text: Combine Step 3 with the canonical zigzags of Step 1. By Step 2, the resulting $R$-module isomorphism is induced by the original coprojection maps under the functor of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], so it is the displayed canonical map in the statement. That map is $A$-linear because each map $H^n(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\iota_i)$ is $A$-linear, and a bijective $A$-linear map has an $A$-linear inverse. Its naturality in the diagram follows from functoriality of tensor, colimits, and cohomology. For a chain map $u:M\to M'$ of $A$-complexes, clause (3) of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] gives a natural transformation represented on each K-flat resolution $F$ by $1_F\otimes u$; its compatibility with the coprojections $\iota_i$ makes the square between the two canonical colimit maps commute. Thus their inverses are natural in $M$ as well.

lean.statement: theorem filteredColimit_derivedTensor_cohomology (f : R →+* A) (I : Type u) [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (n : ℤ) : let QR := (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) let T := Classical.choose (exists_derivedTensor_second_factor_functor f).2 let H := fun M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ ↦ QR ⋙ T.obj M ⋙ homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) n (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (N : I ⥤ CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ), IsIso (colimit.post N (H M))) ∧ (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (N : I ⥤ CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (j : I), colimit.ι (N ⋙ H M) j ≫ colimit.post N (H M) = (H M).map (colimit.ι N j)) ∧ (∀ (M M' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (g : M ⟶ M') (N : I ⥤ CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ), let η := whiskerRight (whiskerLeft QR (T.map g)) (homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) n) colim.map (whiskerLeft N η) ≫ colimit.post N (H M') = colimit.post N (H M) ≫ η.app (colimit N)) ∧ (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (N N' : I ⥤ CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (a : N ⟶ N'), colim.map (whiskerRight a (H M)) ≫ colimit.post N' (H M) = colimit.post N (H M) ≫ (H M).map (colim.map a))
